candidates.evidence:

The Recursive Agents Hackathon
San Francisco, CASat, Oct 17 at 9:00 AM – 10:00 PM (PDT)

Build a team of agents you can walk away from.

During the PyTorch Conference in San Francisco, build agents that can take a goal and run with it. Let them make the plan, spin up sub-agents, delegate work, communicate with each other, check their own progress, recover when things break, and keep going.

Get a head start. Crusoe is hosting Field Day the day before the hackathon. You'll join a random team and race to take a model from raw data to production. Friday, Oct 16, 1-5pm. Spots are limited, register here!

Push beyond the one-shot agent into persistent loops that rarely need you involved: agents building teams and handling delegation, memory, and long-running inference that can keep operating after you walk away until the work is complete

Build on Crusoe Managed Inference and put leading open models, including NVIDIA’s Nemotron family, into production on high-performance NVIDIA infrastructure.

Compete to win $25,000 in cash prizes and an NVIDIA RTX 5090.

Note: This event is fully in-person in San Francisco. Teams may have up to four members. All attendees must apply and be approved to attend.

Register

About Event
​The Builder Base: Buildathon

​Your idea. Your stack. Your build.

​Welcome to The Builder Base: Buildathon — a one-day gathering in San Francisco for engineers, AI builders, founders, designers, and technology professionals who want to spend a full day turning ideas into working products.

​Builder Base is built around one simple idea: give builders the space, tools, people, and time to build.

​Whether you're experimenting with an AI agent, launching a developer tool, creating an enterprise workflow, building a data product, automating a painful process, or working on something completely unconventional, this is your base for the day.

​Come with an idea, a problem, a technology you want to explore — or nothing more than the desire to build. Find teammates, get feedback from experienced builders, learn from industry experts, and ship something you're proud of.

​Event Details

​When: 9:30 AM – 7:00 PM, 30 October 2026
Where: San Francisco, CA
Format: One-day, in-person buildathon
Who: Engineers, AI Builders, Founders, Product Managers, Designers, Data Scientists, and Technology Professionals
Theme: Open-ended — Build what matters

​What to Expect

​A full day dedicated to building

​Turn an idea into a functional prototype

​Collaborate with engineers, founders, designers, and AI practitioners

​Meet potential teammates and future collaborators

​Mentorship and guidance from experienced industry professionals

​Access to modern AI tools, APIs, platforms, and developer resources

​Partner credits, challenges, and special prizes

​Live product demos and project showcases

​Networking with San Francisco's technology and startup community

​Food, refreshments, swag, and prizes

​What Can You Build?

​Anything worth building.

​Build an AI application, autonomous agent, developer tool, enterprise workflow, data platform, automation system, productivity tool, consumer product, infrastructure project, or an idea nobody has tried before.

​There are no prescribed problem statements and no requirement to build around a particular technology.

​Find a problem. Build the solution. Ship it.

​You can arrive with a fully formed idea or figure it out once you get there. The goal is to spend the day building, experimenting, learning, and turning an idea into something real.

​Who Should Join?

​The Builder Base is for people who make things.

​Whether you're an experienced software engineer, an AI developer exploring agentic systems, a founder testing a new idea, a product manager turning a concept into a prototype, a designer bringing an experience to life, or a student and early-career developer looking for your next challenge — you're welcome.

​You don't need to be an expert. You just need to be ready to build.

​Come with an idea. Leave with a build.

About Event

​EDIT: This was supposed to be on Oct 3 but is getting delayed because both cohosts are sick :(

​Bubble Lab and Lunatechs is happy to present to you guys our 2026 PRE-SF Tech Week event! We know everyone is SUPER excited for tech week so we designed what hopefully will be the PERFECT event to kick it off!

​We're bringing this event to you in partnership with the European Startup Embassy, Europe's base in Silicon Valley — a Bay Area hub where European founders land, work, and plug into the US market.

​What is Pretty Cool Demos and Pre-Tech Week Social?

​First we'll do what we're calling "Pretty Cool Demos!". This will be an open demo sign up list where each person gets 5 minutes to show their demo. Skip the long slow roll dramatic story, just cut to the chase and show us the AMAZING thing you are building! Get to know what each other is doing and help each other connect during Tech Week.

​We'll also have a system to share your interests and the Bubble Lab AI system will help us all find potential crew mates! Having a good crew will not only make Tech Week 10x more effective but also make it 10x more enjoyable! We all know that social awkwardness of going to events!

​Agenda

​6:00pm - Check-in

​6:15pm - Introductions - Selina Li and Hanley Leung

​6:25pm - Lucky Drop Prize Game - PRIZES TO BE ANNOUNCED!

​6:30pm - 5 Minute Demo's Begin

​7:00pm - Pre-Tech Week Social w/ AI Matching

​7:30pm - Speakers (TBD/OPTIONAL)

​8:30pm - Lucky Drop Prize Game #2 - PRIZES TO BE ANNOUNCED!

​9:00pm - wrap up

​The Demo Lineup So Far!

​Hanley - Lucky Drop 3.0 - Battle Royale Prize Game!

​Mike Chop - Code.Blue - Making Stroke Obsolete

​Matthew Ao - Space (a16z speedrun) - Infinity Space for Computer

​Carlo Pizzuti - Rolling Around - making bikepacking easier

​Ira Puteri - Legali AI - trauma informed companion for women navigating abuse

​Elvin Atwine - Klo - an agentic video editor

​Garett Brennan - Epoch Trade - AI quant researcher

​Bhanu Kowshik - TBD

​Shutian Cheng - TryOffice - Tracking your leads' buying signals

​YOU

​YOU

​YOU

​SIGN UP PEOPLE! Let's Go!

​Who's this event for?

​Founders, Builders, Dreamers, VC and Angels, looking to get some elevator pitch practice, and "looking for crew" for SF Tech Week. No technical level requirements. Just a passion for technology , AI and desire to change the world!

​What to Bring?

​Yourself, your enthusiasm, your passion, and just be ready to meet great people! Learn, Share, Help, Connect! If you want to give a demo see below on how to add yourself to the list. We'll have an app you can connect to before you arrive, that will be sent to approved attendees.

​How to sign up to Demo?

​Demo's are totally optional but we highly encourage everyone to sign up. We'll set up the demo line by whoever signs up first and also picking out a few special ones to go first. Please contact HANLEY by:

​email info@lunatechs.social

​WhatsApp / iMessage: +1 650 4318036

​IG: @hanleyleung

​And send him the following:

​mention: Pretty Cool Demos Event

​demo title

​one sentence description

​URL to slides/demo so ideally we can have it ready for you on our laptop

​Any special instructions of extra requirements on the computer such as files to download, logged into what accounts, etc

​if you need to use your own computer that's ok too but let us know before hand, we try to minimize computer swapping to keep the pace up

​Who Is Bubble Lab?

​Bubble Lab (YC W26) is the operating system for paid professional communities — member directory, applications, onboarding, matchmaking and engagement workflows in one place, built around Slack and compatible with Discord, WhatsApp and the rest of your stack. Communities show up juggling ~14 tools and about 20 hours a week of manual admin; Bubble Lab replaces the lot.

​It's built by Selina Li and Zach Zhong, a second-time founding duo out of Cornell Tech. Selina went UPenn → quant researcher at J.P. Morgan Asset Management → CEO; Zach went UCSD CS → founding engineer at CutiePet → CTO. Before Bubble Lab they shipped gymii.ai together, an AI nutrition tracker that reached thousands of users through Cornell Tech's Spinouts program. Two people, in San Francisco, out-shipping teams many times their size.

​Who is Lunatechs?

​A tech-enthusiast community — find your fellow tech lunatics. Talks, workshops, meetups, hackathons; no gatekeeping, no monthly commitment. Born in Hong Kong, now 1,000+ members there, with chapters in Hong Kong and Singapore. After Shanghai the tour hits San Francisco, Dallas, Houston, Los Angeles and Palo Alto — Shanghai gets to open it.

​Lunatechs is run by people who've shipped things you've used. Co-founder Hanley Leung is an engineering leader out of Apple, EA and Yahoo!. Co-founder Jason Xu built product at Google and Alibaba. Between them: decades in big tech, and years of hands-on experience working in China's tech world — this isn't a fly-in event; it's a community run by people who know Shanghai's builders are among the best anywhere.

​Who is the European Startup Embassy?

​"Europe's base in Silicon Valley." A Bay Area hub giving European startups and investors a physical and virtual foothold in the US: coworking and event space, a coliving residence, an online community, and hands-on help with market entry, customer acquisition and raising from US VCs. Led by CEO Vladimira Cincurova.

​The details

​Time and Date: Saturday. Oct 3rd, 6pm - 10pm
Venue: European Startup Embassy, 461 Bryant St, San Francisco

​​Find us

​Bubble Lab ​www: https://bubblelab.ai
Bubble Lab email: hello@bubblelab.ai

​Lunatechs ​www: https://lunatechs.social
Lunatechs email: info@lunatechs.social

Location
European Startup Embassy
461 Bryant St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA

​Venture Mindset Hackathon - Reinvent Yourself in SF - builders, founders and judges: GSB/MSx, YC ...

​⏰ Doors open at 11:00 AM sharp.
🚪 Entry closes at 11:15 AM or once we’re full — come early!

​🚀 Join us on January 17 (Sat), 2026 in downtown SF for a one-day Hackathon focused on bold ideas, teamwork, and innovation.

​Participants create a clear vision of who they want to become in 10 years — not in a linear way, but in an exponential, ambitious way, similar to how venture investors think about long-term growth.

​✨ Why it matters:

​GSB/MSx alumni will see how the younger generation learns to think in true Stanford GSB style — with courage, long-term vision, and strategic imagination.

​✅ Challenge:
Create the ultimate AI sales copilot!
This hackathon is for developers, product managers, sales engineers, marketers, and AI enthusiasts who want to reinvent how sales teams work using AI.

​🔧 Choose the sales pain point you want to solve:

​qualifying and prioritizing leads,

​automating repetitive follow-ups,

​optimizing sales funnels,

​or giving teams real-time AI coaching during calls.

​🎯 The main goal is to build a working app or prototype that empowers sales teams, saves time, and drives measurable revenue impact.

​

​

About Event
​Who Killed the Build? 💀

​A Halloween DevTools Murder Mystery with Flox

​The build is dead. The cause? Unknown.

​Join AI Valley and Flox for a Halloween devtools night where you’ll investigate what went wrong, follow the clues, and figure out who (or what) killed the build.

​Instead of a traditional product demo, Flox will take us through an interactive investigation of a broken development environment. Along the way, you’ll uncover suspicious dependencies, environment issues, and other clues before making your final guess.

​🔎 Investigate the crime scene
💻 See Flox in action
🕵️ Follow the clues and solve the mystery
🎃 Enjoy Halloween food, drinks, and networking

​Costumes are encouraged. Production incidents are not.

​Meet the Speakers

​Justin Castilla — Flox

​Jessica Garson Beauchemin — Runpod

​Amin Karbas — Resolve AI

​Dan Gross — FriendliAI

​Agenda

​5:00–6:00 PM — Doors Open + Halloween Food, Drinks & Networking

​6:00–6:10 PM — The Crime Scene: Welcome from AI Valley + Flox and meet the speakers

​6:10–6:50 PM — The Investigation: Talks and demos with Justin Castilla (Flox), Jessica Garson Beauchemin (Runpod), Amin Karbas (Resolve AI), and Dan Gross (FriendliAI), with clues revealed throughout

​6:50–7:00 PM — Solve the Murder: Review the evidence and vote on what killed the build

​7:00–7:10 PM — The Reveal: Uncover the culprit + how Flox helps prevent the underlying problem

​7:10–8:00 PM — Halloween Mixer + Food, Drinks & Networking

​About HAC
Hanwha AI Center (HAC) is a private membership for all those dedicated to AI. As a hub for innovation, HAC brings together passionate entrepreneurs, researchers, and visionaries to explore the societal and technological impacts of AI on human life.

​Flox is a developer tool that creates reproducible, hash-pinned software environments across laptops, CI pipelines, and production. It eliminates environment drift by using a single configuration file to lock exact software versions everywhere. Flox is powered by the Nix package manager, but simplifies the experience so users do not have to write Nix code directly.

​AI Valley is a community rooted in supporting exceptional first generation builders, founders, and creators. We curate environments where ambitious people meet collaborators, mentors, and opportunities through hackathons, workshops, and intimate gatherings across AI, tech, and the arts. If you care about who you build with as much as what you build, this is your place.
